title.narrative: Supporting vulnerable households and conflict affected communities to meet basic needs in the east and south of Ukraine

description.narrative: Impact: To ensure the immediate multisectoral basic needs of vulnerable populations are met and sustained, contributing to their transition from emergency relief to recovery and resilienceOutcome: Emergency basic needs of war-affected populations in Ukraine are addressed through multipurpose cash, in-kind support, shelter, and winter assistance, while capacities of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and community-based responses are strengthened to enable

In response to the needs highlighted within the HNRP, and through our own assessments and project monitoring results within the current GFFO funded project, we are proposing the following activities to enable JERU to provide continued assistance to the most vulnerable war affected individuals:Multipurpose cash assistance,Winterization assistance,In-kind emergency response (hygiene and food kits),Emergency shelter repairs,Psychosocial support,Protection-related community awareness raising and referral mechanisms,Group cash transfers to community-based organizations.

Internally Displacesd Persons (IDPs) (55%), Host community (42%), Returnees (3%) - needs based and subject to change.Multi Purpose Cash Assistance : 39,000 individuals (15,116 households, based on Cash Working Group-endorsed household size of 2.58), receiving cash assistance of 3,600 UAH (approx. 62EUR) per month/person, for 3 months. In-kind assistance: 96,000 unique beneficiaries (32,000 households) supported with in-kind assistance through the provision of Ready-to-Eat kits (10,000) and hygiene kits (22,000 household HKs and 4,400 PSN kits), delivered through partners in response to emergencies. No overlap are expected between recipients of hygiene kits and food kits.Winterization: 11,792 individuals (5,360 households) supported with winterization assistance for 5 months between October and March. Out of these 5,360 households, 4,710 will receive winter cash support in the form of monthly transfers of 149 EUR to cover their winter utilities needs and 650 will be supported with in-kind assistance in the form of solid fuel provision. About 30% of the most vulnerable households will also be receiving MPCA assistance. Emergency Shelter repairs: Approximatively 165 individuals (75 households) will be assisted with light or medium shelter repairs (either in cash or in kind).Protection: 8,360 individuals benefit from groups and individual PSS sessions. 1,584 vulnerable individuals supported with referrals to relevant internal and external services. 5,160 individuals will be targeted by community awareness raising events on protection issues and access to protection services. Community Response Mechanisms: 50 community-based and volunteer groups will received Group Cash Transfers to implement local initiatives in response to community needs.Capacity building of partners: 30 implementing partners' staff are trained throught he organization of workshops.
